rationale: B) 34% reduction in breast cancer mortality, 24% reduction in disease recurrence, 41% reduction in all-cause mortality is correct: The 2011 meta-analysis of more than 12,000 women with breast cancer found that physical activity was associated with a 34% reduction in risk of death from breast cancer, a 24% reduction in disease recurrence, and a 41% reduction in all-cause mortality. These figures are a frequent exam target precisely because the three numbers are easily transposed. A) 24% reduction in breast cancer mortality is incorrect: 24% is the reduction in disease recurrence, not disease-specific mortality — this option swaps the first two outcome figures. C) 41% reduction in disease recurrence is incorrect: 41% is the all-cause mortality reduction; this option transposes the recurrence and all-cause mortality figures. D) 41% reduction in breast cancer mortality is incorrect: 41% corresponds to all-cause mortality, not disease-specific mortality; this option places the largest figure in the wrong outcome category.

question_text: A public health department is prioritizing interventions to reduce premature mortality at a population level. The department cites data indicating that the majority of preventable premature deaths in the United States are attributable to a small number of modifiable factors. Approximately what percentage of all premature deaths are attributable to the combined burden of tobacco use, poor diet and physical inactivity, and alcohol consumption?
rationale: C) 40% is correct: The cited data indicate that 40% of all premature deaths are attributable to three modifiable behavioral factors: tobacco use (18.1%), poor diet and physical activity (16.6%), and alcohol consumption (2.5%). This finding establishes the foundation for lifestyle medicine's role in reducing population-level mortality. A) 18% is incorrect: 18.1% is the contribution of tobacco use alone — the largest single contributor — and candidates who anchor on that figure may not add the contributions of diet, physical activity, and alcohol. B) 27% is incorrect: This intermediate value is not supported by the evidence and likely represents an estimate produced by adding tobacco (18.1%) and alcohol (2.5%) while omitting the diet and physical activity contribution (16.6%). D) 55% is incorrect: This overestimates the combined burden and has no basis in the cited data; candidates may generate this figure by conflating premature death statistics with broader estimates of lifestyle-attributable chronic disease burden.

question_text: A 62-year-old man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, and prediabetes asks his cardiologist which specific dietary pattern has the strongest randomized controlled trial evidence for reducing major cardiovascular events. His cardiologist references the PREDIMED trial. Compared to a reduced-fat dietary pattern, what was the approximate reduction in major cardiovascular events in participants assigned to a Mediterranean dietary pattern supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil?
rationale: D) 30% is correct: The PREDIMED trial found that the incidence of major cardiovascular events was 30% lower among participants assigned to a Mediterranean dietary pattern supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil, and 28% lower among those assigned to the Mediterranean diet supplemented with nuts, compared to a reduced-fat control dietary pattern. These figures represent the strongest RCT evidence supporting a dietary pattern for primary cardiovascular prevention. A) 15% is incorrect: This underestimates the PREDIMED effect size for the EVOO arm and does not correspond to any outcome reported in the trial — it may represent a candidate's intuitive estimate of a modest dietary effect. B) 22% is incorrect: This figure is not derived from the PREDIMED trial and serves as an intermediate-value distractor for candidates who recall that the effect was substantial but do not know the precise figure. C) 28% is incorrect: 28% is the cardiovascular event reduction in the PREDIMED nuts arm, not the extra-virgin olive oil arm — candidates who recall that both arms outperformed the control but do not distinguish between them will select this.
